Paths to close WITHOUT --force: (a) land a83f or 3d57 (either shortens/removes the fence failure), then sign; or (b) opportunistically re-run review-plan in a calmer window -- 75% of single attempts already land a stable ~10s window -- via the cached-sidecar replay (no new LLM spend). --force will not be used.

# Generic, config-driven mapping seam for per-project tracker workflow variance

## Context / Problem

rebar's reconciler hardcodes how its model maps onto a target Jira project's model,
so a project whose workflow lacks an analogous concept cannot be supported without a
core edit — the anti-pattern this epic exists to remove (core rebar must stay
project-agnostic; a single project's states/types must never be named in shipped
code). The mappings live in
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`
(`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`, `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`,
`RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `UNSYNCED_RELATIONS`) and are duplicated in
`config.py` (`local_to_jira_status`, `jira_to_local_status`, `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`) and
`inbound_fields.py` (`_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`,
`_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL`). A live probe of the REB project (Jira Cloud) confirms
the variance is real: REB has a `Blocked` status and an `Initiative` issue type at
`hierarchyLevel` 2 above `Epic` at 1, and no `Supersedes` link type.

The felt need spans four target axes — **status, ticket type, permissible transitions,
and permissible parent relationships** — plus two hardcoded sibling value axes
(**link relations, priority**) and the **required-create-fields** gotcha that hard-fails
`create` on a mandatory custom field.

## Approach

Introduce a **provider-neutral, config-driven mapping seam** read from hand-editable
`rebar.toml`/`[tool.rebar]` config (rebar's config surface per `docs/config.md`), with
the current hardcoded maps preserved as the **built-in default** (lowest precedence).
Config is layered: built-in default → config `default` block → per-project overlay
(`projects.<JIRA_KEY>`), deep-merged per key so an override changes only the keys it
names. The seam is factored onto rebar's existing vendor-adapter boundary
(`docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`, amended by
`docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md`; `_backend.py` `select_backend` /
`OutboundMapper`/`InboundMapper`): a **provider-neutral core** owns the schema, the
layered merge, fail-closed validation, the mapping-application semantics, and a
**capability descriptor** (which axes a target has); a **Jira adapter** supplies
the built-in defaults, the live probe, and the capability values. No other provider is
built here; neutrality is structural, so a future adapter reuses the core untouched.

For target concepts with no analogue, the seam offers four provider-neutral answers,
each building on existing rebar primitives (`rebar-status:` labels,
`EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`, the per-hop
`transition_issue_by_name` call), while S6's replay algorithm itself is new code: **map**
to a chosen value; **collapse** (non-injective, e.g. `epic→Initiative`) made
round-trip-safe by a `rebar-type:` label symmetric with today's `rebar-status:` labels;
**skip** (type-granular whole-ticket exclusion, extending
`EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`); or **drift** with a warning (unrepresentable
statuses/transitions/parents diverge and are recorded, never silently forced). Non-allowed
**transitions** additionally attempt **replay**: S6 adds **new** dispatcher logic that
derives the intended local hop sequence from
the ticket's **core STATUS event log** (per-ticket status-change events already persisted
by the core; the reconciler stores no hop history of its own), anchors
on Jira's current status, and re-attempts each intermediate hop through that existing
single-hop primitive **exactly once each, in recorded order**, aborting to **drift** on
the first hop the target rejects (no retries, no self-invented hops) — so replay is
bounded by the finite recorded hop sequence. When no recorded trail survives — e.g. a
**compacted** ticket whose STATUS events are folded into a snapshot that keeps only the
final status — replay is not applicable and the failed transition degrades to the pre-S6
per-mutation soft-fail backstop (never inventing hops). Non-representable **parents**
additionally leave an echo-safe **breadcrumb comment** naming the nearest represented
ancestor's Jira key. rebar's own transitions and hierarchy are never restricted by a
target's rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A project whose config declares no overrides syncs **byte-for-identical** to
  today's behavior — verified by the existing reconciler suite passing unchanged and a
  test asserting the composed default map equals the current hardcoded constants.
- [x] A per-project overlay changes only the keys it names, layering over the `default`
  block which layers over the built-in default — verified by a config-effect contrast
  test (default vs. overlaid value produce different observable outbound mappings).
- [x] Every mapping axis (status, type, link relation, priority) is driven by the
  config seam rather than a hardcoded literal, with the built-in default as fallback —
  verified by tests that a non-default config value reaches the outbound/inbound differ.
- [x] A rebar type with no target analogue can be **collapsed** (round-trip-safe via a
  `rebar-type:` label) or **skipped** (whole-ticket), and an unmapped-non-skipped type
  **fails closed at config load** — verified per child.
- [x] A non-allowed **transition** is attempted by **replay** of rebar's recorded hops
  and, failing that (or when no recorded trail survives, e.g. a compacted ticket),
  **drifts** — never restricting rebar's local
  transitions — verified per child.
- [x] A non-representable **parent** drifts and leaves an **echo-safe breadcrumb**
  naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key — verified per child.
- [x] Required-field create failures are prevented by a per-project
  `create_defaults` block — verified per child.
- [x] A `rebar bridge suggest-mapping` command interrogates a live target and emits
  suggested config for every offline-discoverable axis, flagging transitions as
  best-effort — verified per child.
- [x] `rebar doctor` detects Jira-compat config problems (offline validation failures
  and live-drift against the target) — verified per child.
- [x] The mapping core is **provider-neutral**: the schema, layered merge, validation,
  application semantics, and capability descriptor contain no Jira-specific literal;
  Jira specifics live only in the adapter — verified by a test that the core modules
  neither import the Jira adapter nor carry Jira value literals.

## Child decomposition (each criterion maps to ≥1 child; responsibilities do not overlap)

- **S1 — Config schema + layered-merge core + capability descriptor** delivers the
  provider-neutral foundation, layering, fail-closed validation framework, and the
  neutrality guarantee.
- **S2 — Status mapping via the seam** retires the three hardcoded status copies to the
  seam, default-preserving.
- **S3 — Type mapping: collapse + `rebar-type:` label + operator skip** delivers the
  no-analogue-type answers and load-time fail-closed on undecided types.
- **S4 — Link-relation mapping** retires
  `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`/`UNSYNCED_RELATIONS` (skip-not-approximate preserved).
- **S5 — Priority mapping + `create_defaults` injection** retires
  `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` to the seam (map-or-drift soft field) and injects
  per-project create_defaults to prevent required-field create failures.
- **S6 — Transition replay** adds a **new** direct→replay→drift fallback to the
  dispatcher, deriving the hop sequence from the core per-ticket STATUS event log
  (drift when that trail is absent, e.g. compaction).
- **S7 — Parent breadcrumb comment** adds the echo-safe nearest-represented-ancestor
  breadcrumb on parent drift.
- **S8 — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping` command** interrogates a live target and emits
  suggested config (the verb is `suggest-mapping`, not `probe`, which collides with the
  retired `bridge-probe` alias).
- **S9 — Docs + `project.portability`** documents the seam + portability guard.
- **S10 — Jira-compat config diagnostics in `doctor`** detects offline-invalid config
  and live-drift.
